title: L’élevage de la crevette tropicale
bookshelves: Category: Technology, Engineering, Agriculture, Industrial processes
summary: With an annual growth rate of around 5% between 2015 and 2026, the shrimp industry supplies products that are widely available in stores, making it a pillar of aquaculture. This industry is expanding and intensifying its operations in coastal areas, particularly in tropical regions. However, this growth trajectory—based on practices and production methods inherited from the 1980s—poses numerous environmental, economic, and societal problems, calling into question the sector’s sustainability: the emergence of animal diseases, as well as significant impacts on coastal ecosystems. To better understand the sector’s current risks and challenges, the author reviews the experience gained in various regions of the world (New Caledonia, Indonesia, Vietnam) regarding the links between shrimp farming and the environment. He discusses the implementation of innovative tools for the monitoring and sustainable management of systems, the diversification of farmed species, the ecological intensification of production systems, the development of integrated multitrophic aquaculture, as well as the rehabilitation of aquaculture ponds abandoned by farmers following successive crises since the 1990s. This book is intended for all stakeholders in the shrimp industry: government officials and their decentralized agencies, local governments, consulting firms, as well as industry professionals—from production to the food processing sector. It also serves as a valuable resource for students and anyone interested in understanding the challenges facing the industry and the solutions being considered to promote more sustainable shrimp farming.
